subject: Emergency: CA rollback & tenant pin safety plan
messages:
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: security@finbank.com, ops@finbank.com
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: CA compromise detection — proposed rollback & tenant-pin safety plan

Team,

Security notified us this morning that a third-party CA we rely on for a subset of on-prem tenant certs may show anomalous issuance patterns. FinBank's security team copied in their ops channel — they asked for a coordinated rollback plan for tenant-specific certificate pins so clients aren't left with hard failures.

Attached are an initial rotation playbook and an impact matrix. High-level proposal:

1) Pause new pin deployments and immediately mark the existing CA as suspect in our internal catalog.
2) For tenants with pinning enabled (FinBank included), deploy a fast rollback that removes strict pin enforcement on our client side while retaining certificate validation (i.e., accept chain validated by existing trusted roots but do not enforce pin).
3) Simultaneously provision new certificates from an alternate, pre-vetted CA and pre-stage CSRs for each tenant. Use the csr-template.txt attached.
4) Update split-DNS CNAME targets for on-prem proxies to point to the new cert-serving endpoint in a staged rollout (canary group = 5% of connections per tenant). TTL considerations below.
5) Enable OCSP stapling on the new endpoints and publish a targeted advisory to customer ops with exact rollback/rollback-undo commands.

Open questions for the group:
- DNS TTL windows we should expect from customer resolvers? FinBank ops said they can push a 60s TTL change for the canary zone.
- Required compliance/legal signoffs for temporarily relaxing pin checks (Laura, please advise).

Given the security sensitivity, I propose we treat this as an emergency change and start the pre-provisioning steps immediately after approval.

Attachments: rotation-playbook.pdf, impact-matrix.csv, csr-template.txt

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Security (Sales Ops)
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CA compromise detection — proposed rollback & tenant-pin safety plan

Marissa — thanks for the writeup, this looks good. Two quick clarifying items before I greenlight pre-provisioning: 

1) When you say "remove strict pin enforcement", do you mean a client-side config toggle we can flip per-tenant, or do we need a code push? If it's a toggle, ops can do it via feature-flag.
2) OCSP stapling: for on-prem TLS proxies that terminate at the tenant edge, can we ensure stapling for the canary without impacting non-canary traffic?

If both are feature-flag and endpoint changes respectively, I approve moving forward with pre-provisioning CSRs and creating the INF ticket; we will hold the actual DNS switch until Karthik confirms canary orchestration.

Ben Carter
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: CA compromise detection — proposed rollback & tenant-pin safety plan

Ben/Marissa — technical details and orchestration notes below. I built the plan assuming we want zero client-code changes for canary and a feature-flag toggle for the wider rollback.

Plan details:
- Pin toggle: we have a per-tenant runtime flag (TENANT_TLS_PIN_MODE) exposed in dedicated and private runtimes. Flipping it to "lenient" will keep full chain verification but skip strict SPKI-pin checks. No code push needed; ops can change via the console/API.
- CSRs: We'll generate per-tenant CSRs using the attached csr-template.txt. For FinBank, use the SAN pattern: CN=tenant.finbank.internal, SAN=tenant1.finbank.internal,tenant1-api.finbank.internal. This preserves existing FQDNs so no client cert updates are required.
- ACME / external CA: We will use our pre-vetted CA pool (CA-B). We'll request short-lived certs (7 day TTL) for initial canary. Once validated, we issue a 90-day cert and rotate to HSM-backed private keys.
- DNS and TTLs: Canary plan uses a shadow host record under tenant zone: canary-ep.tenant1.finbank.internal -> new-proxy-ep.redwood.net. FinBank confirmed they can push 60s TTL. We will keep the original records available and perform canary via weighted DNS (5% weight for canary entry).
- OCSP: New endpoints will advertise stapling. For on-prem proxies that can't staple, we'll fall back to short TTL and revocation-list checks.
- Rollback steps: If canary shows >0.5% TLS errors above baseline, immediately revert weight to 0% and flip TENANT_TLS_PIN_MODE back to strict.

Operational actions to start now (pre-provisioning):
1) Create INF ticket and attach CSR list (I'll open INF-4782).
2) Pre-generate CSRs and send package to FinBank ops for their CA ingestion.
3) Schedule a 2-hour emergency change window for the full rollout if canary is green.

I've opened INF-4782 for tracking: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4782. I'll attach the generated CSRs to that ticket.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Marissa/Karthik/Ben — legal & compliance signoff: temporary relaxation of pin enforcement for operational continuity is acceptable under our emergency CA-incident policy provided: 

1) We maintain full chain validation and do not accept self-signed certs.
2) We notify impacted customers within 24 hours with a change log and an expected remediation timeline.
3) We capture an audit trail for the pin toggle change and the exact tenant identifiers affected.

Please ensure the INF ticket contains: customer acknowledgement (FinBank ops note), the CSR bundle, and the exact timestamps for when TENANT_TLS_PIN_MODE will be toggled. I authorize proceeding with pre-provisioning and canary steps once INF-4782 includes those items.

I'll coordinate with GRC for the post-incident writeup.

Laura Bennett
